title: R136 observed with WFC3
caption: The star cluster R136 in the Tarantula Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: R136, RMC 136 · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, P Crowther (University of Sheffield)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Hubble looks here into the heart of the Tarantula Nebula, which lies in the Large Magellanic Cloud. At lower right sits R136, a young, dense star cluster packed with hundreds of young blue stars. Among them is the most massive star yet detected in the Universe.

Using Hubble, astronomers studied the central, densest part of R136 in detail and found nine stars each weighing more than 100 times the mass of the Sun. The Large Magellanic Cloud is a small companion galaxy of the Milky Way, and the Tarantula Nebula within it is a vast cloud of gas where new stars are forming.

Stars of such enormous mass are rare and burn through their fuel quickly, so finding a group of them together offers a valuable chance to learn how the most massive stars form and live. Hubble's sharp view is what makes it possible to separate them in such a crowded cluster.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.65 x 2.63 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 131 × 130 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using ultraviolet, visible, hydrogen-alpha and near-infrared filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of this light is ultraviolet or near-infrared and invisible to the eye, and Hubble's sharpness separates individual stars in a crowded cluster in another galaxy.

explore: R136 lies about 170,000 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Dorado. The image was made with Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 through filters ranging from ultraviolet to near-infrared, including one that isolates glowing hydrogen.
alt: The central Tarantula Nebula, with a dense cluster of blue stars at lower right.
